Not affected: this DoS was introduced by a Python 3.8 change that replaced http.client’s chunked _safe_read implementation with an unbounded read based on Content-Length, and it was later reverted in the 3.9 branch (3.9.5). Python 3.6 retains the earlier _safe_read loop that reads in bounded chunks (using a MAXAMOUNT cap), so the unbounded allocation path required for exploitation does not exist in that version. Given the target project version is Python 3.6, this CVE does not apply.

statements.action_statement: We’ve reasoned not to port this fix due to the following: - The upstream patch doesn’t change behavior - The official Python patch only adds deprecation warnings; it does not prevent the potentially problematic decoding. The actual behavior change is deferred to a future Python version (3.15+).  - Upstream explicitly declined to backport to older versions for compatibility reasons. See [[https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346|https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346|https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346|https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346]] for more details.

Consequently, the Python 3.9 project is not impacted in this Linux server/VM context.
